title: Janmashtami: the night Krishna was born
hook: a prison at midnight, a river that parts, and a baby carried across it to safety

segments.voice: Yesterday, presented as the tradition's own unresolved argument: the Ramayana serial ended, seven books, a king walking into the river, and a question still open. Did you let one question stay open? Today a new block begins: the festival year. Day six hundred seventy.

It's nearly midnight, and in temples across India, and in living rooms in Houston and Leicester and Singapore, people who have fasted all day are waiting. There's a small cradle decorated with flowers. Someone keeps checking the clock. At twelve, the conch shells blow, the bells ring, and somebody sets a tiny image of a baby into the cradle and starts rocking it. A birthday, kept at the exact hour. To see why midnight, we go to a prison cell.
screen: `A DAY OF FASTING.` → `AN EMPTY CRADLE.` → `AT MIDNIGHT, THE CONCH.`

segments.voice: Janma means birth. Ashtami means the eighth: the eighth day of the waning moon. Janmashtami, the birthday on the eighth. The story is told in the tenth book of the Bhagavata Purana. In Mathura, the tyrant Kamsa is driving his cousin Devaki and her new husband Vasudeva in a chariot after their wedding, when a voice from the sky tells him: the eighth child of this woman will kill you. Kamsa locks them in prison. Child after child is born there, and Kamsa takes them. Then comes the eighth. He is born at midnight, in the dark half of the month, and the Bhagavata says the whole world grows calm and bright at the hour: rivers clear, fires burn steady, the sky full of stars. The baby first appears to his parents in a divine form, then becomes an ordinary newborn. And now Vasudeva's chains fall away. The guards sleep. The prison doors open by themselves. Vasudeva puts the baby in a basket and walks out into a storm. A great serpent, Shesha, spreads its hoods over the basket like an umbrella. He reaches the Yamuna, swollen with rain, and the river gives way to let him through. On the far bank is Gokul, where the cowherd Nanda's wife Yashoda has just given birth. Vasudeva leaves his son there and carries her baby back. By dawn, the prison doors are locked again, as if nothing happened. That's the night people stay up for: the good, arriving in the darkest hour, in the most locked-up place.
screen: `JANMA: BIRTH. ASHTAMI: THE EIGHTH.` · `THE EIGHTH CHILD, BORN IN A PRISON.` · `THE CHAINS FALL. THE RIVER GIVES WAY.` · `A BABY CARRIED TO GOKUL.` · then, large: `THE GOOD ARRIVES AT MIDNIGHT.`

segments.voice: If you can, dim the lights or close your eyes so it's dark. Sit in that darkness and don't hurry it. Notice what the dark does: maybe the ears get sharper, maybe the body gets restless. Then, quietly, wait for something good, without deciding what. A sound, a thought of someone, a softening in the shoulders. Just wait, the way people wait for midnight. The bell holds the time.
Janmashtami. The birthday on the eighth: Krishna's birth at midnight in Kamsa's prison, kept by many Hindus with a fast and a cradle.
Your line: the good arrives at midnight. Tonight, in the latest dark hour you're awake, notice one good thing that turned up anyway. Day six hundred seventy.

screen: `DAY 670 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: GANESH CHATURTHI: WELCOMING GANESHA HOME.`

howItsDone: On Janmashtami many Hindus fast through the day, sing devotional songs in the evening, and at midnight celebrate Krishna's birth with conch shells, bells and a decorated cradle, then break the fast.

original.note: Sanskrit janma (birth) + aṣṭamī (the eighth lunar day): Krishna's birthday.

trapdoor: what you thought: Janmashtami is Krishna's birthday on a fixed date.
what it means: it falls on the eighth day of the waning moon, so the date moves on the solar calendar.
what a scholar hears: the Bhagavata Purana's tenth book tells the birth, and the month is named differently in the two Indian lunar calendars, Shravana in one and Bhadrapada in the other.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.1 (the voice at Devaki's wedding; Kamsa imprisons the couple)

notes: Block D opener (the festival year). Confirm that the Bhagavata places Krishna's birth at midnight and describes the calm, bright world at the hour.
The Yamuna 'gives way': the Bhagavata says the river made way for Vasudeva; popular tellings say it parted or receded. Confirm phrasing.
Month naming: Bhadrapada in the purnimanta calendar, Shravana in the amanta calendar. Confirm.
